caption: Seen from above, a half-wave dipole radiates strongest broadside — out from its sides — and almost nothing off its ends (T9A10). The power is not amplified; it is concentrated. That focusing in a specified direction, compared to a reference antenna, is all antenna “gain” means (T9A11).
spoken: a polar plot of a half-wave dipole's radiation pattern with two lobes broadside to the wire and nulls off the ends, showing gain as concentration rather than amplification
